title: Dynamic Slotting Under Scarce Forward Capacity: A Persistence- and Co-occurrence-Based Heuristic for Semi-Automated Case Picking
content: Semi-automated case picking combines automated pallet transportation with manual retrieval from a capacity-constrained forward area. When stock keeping units (SKUs) outnumber accessible ground-level locations, daily reconfiguration requires deciding which pallets to lower and where to place them. We propose AbLoc, an interpretable heuristic that combines persistent-SKU locations with daily allocation based on pallet-level co-occurrence, known next-day demand, and warehouse state. A stateful industrial trace-driven replay covers 131 working days, 61,113 pallet missions, and 1,480 SKUs competing for 488 positions. Against a structured ablation retaining the same deployed static geography but randomizing dynamic reference-location selection, AbLoc reduces travel in all eight expanding-window folds, by 4.24% on average. Comparisons with conventional policies show reductions of 6.28-8.45%, but these combine static- and dynamic-layer effects and therefore provide operational rather than component-isolating evidence. A historical-affinity refitting diagnostic changes held-out distance by 0.70%, while the tested parameter configurations span 2.34%. Full-horizon accounting reveals a trade-off between travel reductions and the timing of replenishments, rather than universal dominance. Explicit indifference thresholds allow facilities to assess this trade-off using site-specific operating costs.
